rules.scope: Dermoscopy; nonpigmented facial lesions.

reading_note: Read full osteosarcoma etiology window including every incidental syndrome. Separate etiologic definitions, phenotype sets, and cancer-risk associations. Source spelling Rothmund-Thompson is retained. No outside medical correction or invented gene-result sufficiency.

non_target_source.anchor: the most common primary pediatric bone malignancy
non_target_source.reason: Relative frequency and the separate approximate 20% share of primary bone tumors are background prevalence, not a patient-level diagnostic criterion or calibrated prior.

non_target_source.anchor: division into several subtypes according to the degree of differentiation
non_target_source.reason: Classification axes are named, but no concrete subtype-to-feature rule is supplied beyond primary/secondary definitions already inventoried.

non_target_source.anchor: treatment options and survivability have vastly improved
non_target_source.reason: Treatment improvement and survivability do not diagnose osteosarcoma.

non_target_source.anchor: its etiology remains obscure
non_target_source.reason: Etiology research uncertainty and broad factors genetics/epidemiology/environment do not specify an additional disease predicate.

rules.source_anchor: derived from primitive bone-forming (osteoid producing) mesenchymal cells
rules.source_semantics: Osteosarcoma is a malignant bone tumor derived from primitive bone-forming/osteoid-producing mesenchymal cells. Cell lineage describes the disease; any osteoid-producing cell is not automatically osteosarcoma.
rules.scope: Malignant tumor identity, not any normal bone-forming cell.

rules.source_anchor: primary (no underlying bone pathology)
rules.source_semantics: Primary osteosarcoma occurs with no underlying bone pathology. The restriction is scoped to primary form, not all osteosarcoma.
rules.scope: Subtype definition; no independent sufficiency.

rules.source_anchor: secondary forms (underlying pathology which has undergone malignant degeneration/conversion)
rules.source_semantics: Secondary osteosarcoma arises in pre-existing pathology that has undergone malignant degeneration/conversion. Both the antecedent lesion and malignant conversion belong to the subtype relation.
rules.scope: Subtype definition, not all osteosarcoma.

rules.source_anchor: highly complex karyotypes typical of osteosarcoma tumor cytology
rules.source_semantics: Highly complex karyotypes are typical in osteosarcoma tumor cytology, not a necessary single mutation or diagnostic sufficiency.

rules.source_anchor: Hereditary Retinoblastoma: An autosomal dominant condition caused by germline mutations in the RB1 gene
rules.source_semantics: Hereditary retinoblastoma is an autosomal dominant condition due to germline RB1 mutations. Germline context and hereditary subtype are integral.
rules.scope: Hereditary form, not all sporadic retinoblastoma.

rules.source_anchor: causes bilateral retinoblastoma at an average presenting age of one year
rules.source_semantics: The hereditary condition is described with bilateral retinoblastoma at mean presenting age one year. Mean age is not an age requirement and later presentation does not exclude it.
rules.scope: Bilateral/mean-age clause concerns hereditary disorder; general retinoblastoma red-reflex claim is a separate target.

rules.source_anchor: Retinoblastoma characteristically presents as an absence of the "red reflex"
rules.source_semantics: Retinoblastoma characteristically presents with an absent red reflex in the affected eye or eyes; source does not call this individually sufficient or mandatory.
rules.scope: General retinoblastoma sentence within hereditary-retinoblastoma paragraph, not restricted to both eyes.

rules.source_anchor: This disorder imparts an increased risk of osteosarcoma later in life
rules.source_semantics: Hereditary retinoblastoma increases later-life osteosarcoma risk; it does not ensure an osteosarcoma diagnosis.
rules.scope: Later in life relative to childhood retinoblastoma.

rules.source_anchor: Li-Fraumeni Syndrome:An autosomal dominant disorder due to mutations in the p53 tumor suppressor gene
rules.source_semantics: Li-Fraumeni is described as autosomal dominant and caused by p53 tumor-suppressor gene mutations. The source does not state that any nonspecific p53 tumor mutation alone diagnoses the inherited syndrome.

rules.source_anchor: has been found in up to 3% of children with osteosarcoma
rules.source_semantics: Li-Fraumeni has been found in up to 3% of children with osteosarcoma. This is prevalence of the syndrome conditional on pediatric osteosarcoma; it is not P(osteosarcoma|Li-Fraumeni).
rules.scope: Reported upper frequency in children with osteosarcoma; not a calibrated LR.

rules.source_anchor: conveys a predisposition to osteosarcoma

rules.source_anchor: a predilection for osteosarcoma

rules.source_semantics: Inflammatory cardiomyopathy is defined by myocarditis together with ventricular remodeling and cardiac dysfunction. The joint definition must be retained; any one component alone is not stated sufficient.

rules.source_anchor: commonly causes myocarditis, cardiomyopathy, and CHF

rules.source_anchor: Other viral causes of myocarditis and inflammatory cardiomyopathy include

rules.source_anchor: Viruses can also activate autoimmune myocarditis

rules.scope: Autoimmune myocarditis; viral trigger is not proof of myocarditis.

rules.source_semantics: The RV is described as hypertensive in PA-IVS, especially with a competent tricuspid valve, due to inadequate blood egress. Competence is an intensifying scope, not an all-required diagnostic condition.

rules.source_anchor: some parts of the myocardium become dependent on the right ventricle for perfusion, a condition known as RVDCC
rules.source_semantics: RVDCC names the condition in which some myocardium depends on the RV for perfusion, in the described progressive-coronary-stenosis setting. It does not require the entire myocardium to be RV-dependent.
rules.scope: Partial myocardium explicitly sufficient for the name; whole-heart universal requirement is not authorized.
rules.notes: At descriptive representation level, a short predicate such as RV-dependent perfusion of some myocardial regions can preserve the existential scope; formal executable quantifier semantics are not guaranteed.

reading_note: Read all prose and all three criterion bullets. Whole criterion framework is one source rule. Source says two secondary criteria are typically observed but does not state which major/minor combination establishes diagnosis; no all/any/count diagnostic gate may be invented. The codon-816 rule is explicitly broadened by newer guidance.

non_target_source.anchor: only a limited number of laboratories currently possess the capability
non_target_source.reason: Laboratory ability to sequence KIT in skin is availability context, not a disease condition.

rules.source_anchor: In addition to the primary criterion, 2 secondary criteria are typically observed
rules.target: cutaneous mastocytosis (subtype unspecified in actual criterion text)
rules.source_semantics: The visible framework contains typical mastocytosis skin lesions associated with Darier sign (apparent primary item), lesional-skin histologic mast proliferation/increased counts, and an activating KIT mutation in lesional skin (secondary items). A definitive elevated-cell-count threshold is absent and some patients with cutaneous lesions have normal counts, requiring clinical correlation. Historical KIT codon 816 is broadened to activating KIT mutations because additional codons occur in pediatric patients. The text does not define how many primary/minor items must be satisfied to diagnose the condition.
rules.scope: Cutaneous lesional tissue; pediatric 40% additional-codon observation motivates broadening. Not a systemic-mastocytosis criterion set, and title alone cannot make it diffuse-subtype specific.
rules.notes: Primary/minor roles inferred from prose/order, but no complete combination formula. The 40% observation and normal-count exception are retained within this rule rather than counted as leaves. Broadening from codon 816 must not be dropped.

reading_note: Read full DID differential passage, including duplicated line around depression/acute intrusions. Count each distinct source claim once. Differential resemblance does not diagnose a competing disorder; phenomenological differences are nonrigid unless source explicitly supplies a causal discrimination condition.

non_target_source.anchor: diagnostic evaluation after cessation of the crisis can help confirm the diagnosis
non_target_source.reason: Timing of reassessment may help confirmation; cessation of crisis is not itself sufficient to diagnose DID.

rules.source_anchor: Dissociative experiences of identity fragmentation or possession
rules.source_semantics: Identity fragmentation/possession and perceived loss of control over thoughts, feelings, impulses or acts may resemble thought insertion/withdrawal. Resemblance is a differential pitfall, not proof of formal thought disorder.
rules.scope: DID context of the differential section.

rules.source_anchor: may also report visual, tactile, olfactory, gustatory, and somatic hallucinations
rules.source_semantics: DID patients may report visual, tactile, olfactory, gustatory or somatic hallucinations, usually related to posttraumatic/dissociative factors such as partial flashbacks. No modality is required and all modalities need not coexist.

rules.source_anchor: experience these symptoms as caused by alternate identities
rules.source_semantics: The passage describes these hallucination-like symptoms as attributed to alternate identities, without delusional explanations, and often personified. Preserve the symptom-specific scope and differing descriptive strengths; do not turn no delusional explanation into a universal ban on any comorbid delusion.
rules.scope: These symptoms refers to immediately preceding experiences.

rules.source_anchor: Persecutory and derogatory internal voices in dissociative identity disorder associated with depressive symptoms
rules.source_semantics: DID persecutory/derogatory internal voices in conjunction with depressive symptoms can be misdiagnosed as major depression with psychotic features. This warns against treating that combination as sufficient for the competing diagnosis.
rules.notes: Duplicated occurrence in source counted once.

rules.source_anchor: may be distinguished from brief psychotic disorder by the predominance of dissociative symptoms and amnesia for the episode
rules.source_semantics: When chaotic identity changes and acute intrusions disrupt thought, predominance of dissociative symptoms together with episode amnesia can distinguish DID from brief psychotic disorder. The conjunction supports differential discrimination, not a standalone complete DID diagnosis.

rules.source_anchor: if the substance in question is judged to be etiologically related to the disturbance
rules.source_semantics: Symptoms due to physiological substance effects can be distinguished from DID when the substance is judged etiologically related to the disturbance. Mere exposure is not enough; causal attribution is required for this discrimination. The passage does not exclude possible coexisting DID.
rules.scope: Attribution of the observed disturbance, not global comorbidity ban.

rules.source_anchor: often present identities that appear to encapsulate a variety of severe personality disorder feahires
rules.source_semantics: DID identities often appear to encapsulate severe personality-disorder features, suggesting personality-disorder differential, especially borderline. Apparent features do not establish a personality-disorder diagnosis.

rules.source_anchor: the individual’s longitudinal variability in personality style
rules.source_semantics: DID has longitudinal variability of personality style from inconsistency among identities, contrasted with the pervasive/persistent pattern of personality disorders. The longitudinal/identity relationship must be retained.
rules.scope: Longitudinal pattern, not a single assessment.

rules.source_anchor: pervasive and persistent dysfimction in affect management and interpersonal relationships typical of those with personality disorders
rules.source_semantics: Personality disorders typically show pervasive and persistent dysfunction in affect management and interpersonal relationships, contrasted with identity-linked variability in DID. Typical profile is not stated as a sufficient complete diagnosis.

rules.source_anchor: Alvarado Clinical Scoring System
rules.source_semantics: The Alvarado score sums presence/absence-weighted items: RLQ tenderness 2; elevated temperature annotated 37.3 C/99.1 F 1; rebound tenderness 1; migration of pain to RLQ 1; anorexia 1; nausea OR vomiting 1; leukocytosis >10,000 2; leukocyte left shift 1 (maximum 10). Score <=3 makes appendicitis unlikely, not impossible. Scores >=7 recommend surgical consultation, while 4–6 suggest considering CT; neither action threshold is a supplied diagnostic confirmation. Temperature comparator is not explicitly printed and must not be invented.
rules.scope: Score aids management; unlikely is weak negative evidence. Temperature wording retained as a labeled criterion with unstated comparator, not resolved by outside knowledge.
rules.notes: All score components and OR within nausea/vomiting belong to one program. Counting nausea and vomiting twice or hard-excluding at <=3 changes semantics. Management branches retained in the whole program but not counted as separate diagnostic rules.
